Nature of Involvement: Fixed a Google Search Console "Discovered - currently not indexed" issue (238 pages) at user request, from a GSC Coverage Drilldown export the user downloaded and shared. Per Google's own definition this status means Google found the URL but deliberately deferred crawling it to avoid overloading the site -- a crawl-rate/budget signal, not a content-quality judgment. Categorized the 238 URLs: 164 individual BiOrchive exam-question pages, 74 other pages. Ran an Explore pass first to rule out a broken-internal-linking theory: confirmed layouts/shortcodes/question-bank.html and papers-problems.html both server-render real <a href> anchors to every question page (not JS-populated), so linking was never the problem -- this is purely Google's crawl budget. Two fixes, both aimed at shrinking the low-value crawlable URL surface competing for that budget: (1) Added noindex: true + sitemap: {disable: true} to 15 content files -- all 8 content/**/attempt/index.md pages (BiOrchive + BiOClash timed-attempt interfaces) and 7 of 8 content/**/leaderboard/index.md pages (every per-round leaderboard), confirmed via Explore to be thin JS-app-shells (near-empty HTML + Supabase-fetched client-side content), same pattern already proven on account/dashboard/doubts. (2) Disabled Hugo's implicit default categories/tags taxonomies entirely via an empty [taxonomies] table in hugo.toml, after confirming zero content files anywhere set categories:/tags: front matter and zero layouts (site or theme) reference them -- the built output for both was literally just an <h1> and nothing else. Deliberately did NOT add sitemap priority/changefreq tuning, since Google has stated those signals carry little weight in modern crawl decisions -- flagged to the user as a low-value follow-up rather than building it. Verified with a full hugo --gc --cleanDestinationDir build: public/categories/ and public/tags/ no longer exist, sitemap.xml dropped from 640 to 623 URLs (exactly the 15 + 2 expected), the 15 pages correctly render <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">, and /papers/leaderboard/ correctly still renders index,follow. Noted to the user that actual Google re-indexing happens over days-to-weeks as Google reprocesses the sitemap -- not something verifiable synchronously, only the structural fix could be confirmed now. Also recommended (cannot do myself, no GSC access): manually use GSC's Request Indexing for the still-unindexed round-hub pages specifically, prioritized over individual questions, since indexing a hub page lets Google naturally re-crawl the already-linked questions beneath it.

Grepped for the same defect signature across every data/papers/*.yaml file and found it was systemic, not a one-off: 32 occurrences total across data/papers/ibo/2015.yaml (15), 2017.yaml (16), and 2020.yaml (1) -- consistent with a bulk text-rewrap of explanation strings that had a bug wherever a wrap boundary landed immediately before a comma. Fixed by removing the erroneous leading backslash from all 32 lines (script-based, matched only lines whose stripped content starts with backslash-comma, preserving all indentation and surrounding text) -- confirmed via a broader scan that no other invalid-escape variants (only the comma case) existed anywhere in data/papers/. The earlier data/icons.yaml shadowing theory, while disproven, was ruled out empirically before any fix was proposed rather than left as unverified speculation.
